question: What is included in the service desk?
html:
What the service desk includes

Our service desk is built around HELIX, our service-desk product, with a Tier-0 AI agent in front of it. Over the next year we will add two subscriptions on top: a cyber-posture service and legal-AI enablement (Frontline growth plan). Detailed scope, such as hours, response times and per-seat pricing, is not set out in the materials we can draw on here.

The four planned components

ComponentWhat it doesTiming
HELIX service deskMoves from a staffed help desk to a product-led deskPhase 1, months 0-12
Tier-0 AI agentResolves routine requests before they reach a technicianPhase 1
Cyber-posture subscriptionOngoing security-posture service sold alongside the deskPhase 1, after HELIX
Legal-AI enablementHelps firms move AI tools from licence to firm-wide usePhase 1, AM Law base first

(Frontline growth plan)

Who delivers it

  • Support runs on a heavily offshore delivery base in Goa, Hyderabad and Cape Town (Frontline public filings).
  • Staff numbered about 1,100 in January 2026 (Frontline public filings).
  • We support 900+ law-firm clients, according to June 2026 press (Frontline growth plan).

Why legal-AI enablement is included

  • ILTA research finds that 68% of firms have Copilot but only 8% have deployed it firm-wide (Frontline growth plan).
  • That gap is the reason legal-AI enablement sits inside the service relationship rather than being a separate project.

Mid-size firms

  • For mid-size firms we recommend a "bundle" offer. The top-ranked prospects include Weber Gallagher (167 attorneys) and Rivkin Radler (250 attorneys) (Mid-size law firms).
  • The contents of that bundle are not defined in our materials.

What we can't confirm yet

These figures are not in our materials:

  • Coverage hours
  • Response and resolution times
  • Ticket volumes
  • The share of tickets the Tier-0 agent is expected to resolve

A service catalogue, client SLA schedules and twelve months of ticket data would answer these questions.

The plan models EBITDA margin rising from about 15.4% to about 16.7% (est.) by month twelve, driven by Tier-0 deflection and cyber attach. With a $90M term loan in the structure, EBITDA growth has to carry the return, so the desk's scope is a margin decision as much as a product one (Frontline growth plan; Frontline public filings).

Next actions

  1. Publish a one-page service catalogue for HELIX, covering tiers, hours and SLAs, so this answer can be specific.
  2. Pull twelve months of ticket data to baseline the deflection rate the Tier-0 agent must beat.
  3. Define the mid-size "bundle" by naming which of the four components it includes and how it is priced.
  4. Set a firm-wide AI deployment metric for legal-AI enablement clients, measured against the 8% ILTA benchmark.

# What the service desk includes

Our service desk is built around HELIX, our service-desk product, with a Tier-0 AI agent in front of it. Over the next year we will add two subscriptions on top: a cyber-posture service and legal-AI enablement (Frontline growth plan). Detailed scope, such as hours, response times and per-seat pricing, is not set out in the materials we can draw on here.

## The four planned components

| Component | What it does | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| HELIX service desk | Moves from a staffed help desk to a product-led desk | Phase 1, months 0-12 |
| Tier-0 AI agent | Resolves routine requests before they reach a technician | Phase 1 |
| Cyber-posture subscription | Ongoing security-posture service sold alongside the desk | Phase 1, after HELIX |
| Legal-AI enablement | Helps firms move AI tools from licence to firm-wide use | Phase 1, AM Law base first |

*(Frontline growth plan)*

## Who delivers it

- Support runs on a heavily offshore delivery base in Goa, Hyderabad and Cape Town (Frontline public filings).
- Staff numbered about 1,100 in January 2026 (Frontline public filings).
- We support 900+ law-firm clients, according to June 2026 press (Frontline growth plan).

## Why legal-AI enablement is included

- ILTA research finds that 68% of firms have Copilot but only 8% have deployed it firm-wide (Frontline growth plan).
- That gap is the reason legal-AI enablement sits inside the service relationship rather than being a separate project.

## Mid-size firms

- For mid-size firms we recommend a "bundle" offer. The top-ranked prospects include Weber Gallagher (167 attorneys) and Rivkin Radler (250 attorneys) (Mid-size law firms).
- The contents of that bundle are not defined in our materials.

## What we can't confirm yet

These figures are not in our materials:

- Coverage hours
- Response and resolution times
- Ticket volumes
- The share of tickets the Tier-0 agent is expected to resolve

A service catalogue, client SLA schedules and twelve months of ticket data would answer these questions.

The plan models EBITDA margin rising from about 15.4% to about 16.7% (est.) by month twelve, driven by Tier-0 deflection and cyber attach. With a $90M term loan in the structure, EBITDA growth has to carry the return, so the desk's scope is a margin decision as much as a product one (Frontline growth plan; Frontline public filings).

## Next actions

1. Publish a one-page service catalogue for HELIX, covering tiers, hours and SLAs, so this answer can be specific.
2. Pull twelve months of ticket data to baseline the deflection rate the Tier-0 agent must beat.
3. Define the mid-size "bundle" by naming which of the four components it includes and how it is priced.
4. Set a firm-wide AI deployment metric for legal-AI enablement clients, measured against the 8% ILTA benchmark.
